neighbours.label: a bare (article-less) abstract noun of merit or outcome as the object of a weighing/predicting verb or preposition ('offset ⟦benefits⟧ of', 'predict ⟦performance⟧', 'thought given to ⟦efficacy⟧'); the same nouns with an article as subject do not fire
fire: Critics argued that the delays would cancel benefits of the new rail line.
The simulator lets pilots estimate performance and check fuel margins.
The agency approved the vaccine without much attention paid to efficacy in older adults.
Engineers use the model to forecast reliability and plan repairs.
The trial was stopped because rising costs would erase gains from the therapy.
The committee funded the programme with no real thought given to effectiveness.
Farmers want a cheap way to predict yield and judge soil quality.
The review found that the fees would outweigh advantages of the scheme.
quiet: Critics argued that the benefits of the new rail line were obvious.
The performance of the simulator impressed the pilots at the fuel depot.
The efficacy of the vaccine in older adults was approved by the agency.
The reliability of the model surprised the engineers who planned repairs.
The gains from the therapy were clear when the trial was stopped.
The effectiveness of the programme pleased the committee that funded it.
The yield was good and the farmers were happy with the soil.
The advantages of the scheme were listed in the review of the fees.

notes: Card: ' benefits', ' structure', ' evolutionary', ' amount', ' performance', ' efficacy', ' development', ' use', ' ability'. Probes: bare object nouns 0.22-0.54 (efficacy, performance, benefits, structure); 'The benefits of exercise' 0.02, 'the ability of' 0.11, unrelated 0.01.
